claims.claim: zero-growth food 0.03 mg C/L and r_max 0.28/d at 20 °C (Stemberger & Gilbert 1985, via Ramos-Rodríguez et al. 2020)
claims.quote: who reported an rmax of 0.28 day−1 and TFL of 0.03 mg C l−1
claims.conditions: Stemberger & Gilbert 1985's values as reported here: K. cochlearis at 20 °C fed Rhodomonas minuta, 'assuming 50% carbon content of food algae by dry mass'
claims.note: the 'via' attribution is right: Ramos-Rodríguez et al. report S&G's numbers and do not measure at 20 °C. Their own clones (Ruidera lakes, Spain; Cryptomonas pyrenoidifera at 0.026–0.624 mg C/L; 9.7, 15.6 and 18.5 °C) gave TFLs from < 0.03 mg C/L (Tinaja clone, 15.6 °C) to 0.13 mg C/L (18.5 °C), < 0.1 at 9.7 °C, and the Cueva Morenilla clone's TFL was 4× the Tinaja clone's at 15.6 °C (p. 8); the Tinaja clone's rm rose from 0.020/d at 9.7 °C to 0.125/d at 15.6 °C. A Cryptomonas-fed clone's TFL of 0.018 ± 0.004 mg C/L at 20 °C is also cited (Ramos-Rodríguez 2003, p. 4). The threshold is clone- and temperature-dependent, by a factor of 4 or more

claims.claim: ~1 mg C/L saturates K. cochlearis growth (Ramos-Rodríguez et al. 2020)
claims.quote: concentration of 1 mg C l−1 is sufficient to support the maximal growth rate
claims.conditions: said of rotifers in general, citing Stemberger & Gilbert 1985, to justify feeding the stock cultures ~1 mg C/L of Cryptomonas once a week
claims.note: the value is in this source, but as Stemberger & Gilbert 1985's: cite it as '(Stemberger & Gilbert 1985, via Ramos-Rodríguez et al. 2020)'. It is a sufficient level, not a fitted half-saturation constant; the article's own Monod fits (Eq. 1, rm = rmax(C − TFL)/(C − TFL + Ks)) give no Ks at 20 °C

notes: Both values check, and the paper's 'via' attribution is right; in the code comment, the '~1 mg C/L saturates' should also carry 'Stemberger & Gilbert 1985, via'. For the rewrite: the source's own measurements show K. cochlearis's zero-growth food varying about fourfold between two neighbouring clones and between 15.6 and 18.5 °C (p. 8), so 0.03 mg C/L is one clone at 20 °C on Rhodomonas, not a species constant (the authors' introduction says TFLs 'are not species-specific constants'). The code's derived 0.020 'units, 0.6 of Daphnia's' is project arithmetic not checked here.
